newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU vows not to confront Australia on wheat market.
newsitem.headline: EU vows not to confront Australia on wheat market.

text.p: The European Union does not regard itself as a direct competitor of Australia on the world wheat market and is satisified with its recent exports despite a dip in volumes last week, Guy Legras, director general of agriculture at the EU Commission, said on Tuesday.

He told Reuters the EU had rejected most bids to export wheat at last Thursday's weekly auction because they were too low. But there was no question of maximising exports to compete with Australia, widely considered the current market leader.
"We will never do it...The Australians are not on the same markets as us," he said in a telephone interview.
Legras rejected suggestions the EU had been overcautious with an export award of some 70,000 tonnes of wheat last week.
"We have given them (the grain exporters) as much as they wanted. But last week we tightened the screw a bit because they were exaggerating. Their bids were not good last week," he said.
"If we put last week to one side they have been well treated," he said.
Legras said last week's tender had been affected by special factors including the strength of the dollar and the direction of internal prices.
"If they make the right offers, then there won't be a problem," he said.
Legras said the average pace of exports was 300-400,000 tonnes a week and this was nothing to complain about.
"We have sold quite a lot up to now," he said.
Asked about some trade forecasts of a sharp rise in EU intervention stocks if exports did not increase, Legras said some wheat would probably be left behind but not a big amount.
"There will be intervention stocks at the end of the campaign, that is clear. But they won't be gigantic. Everything is fine," Legras said.

Some traders have warned of three to four million tonnes of wheat being dumped into intervention by the May closing date for EU purchases, though forecasts have been made difficult by the lack of data about internal feed consumption.
The EU, which had a bumper crop last autumn, had practically no wheat in intervention when the season began on July 1, 1996.
